notes: New stored edit (very_unlikely), replacing "the largest prime factor of 1729 is 23", a derived edit whose original fact none of the four models held. That a Möbius strip has one side is its best-known property. Mathematics leaves out worlds and the indeterminate query (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number, a shape or a proof rests on definitions, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between; the record has 4 determinate derived queries. Derived queries ask what the edit forces with the definitions held fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. The relation has_surface_sides is functional. The near query ("Does a Möbius strip have only one side?") is the negation of the edit, because the relation has two values; it is kept because the topic needs a functional near query and no other one-hop stored form of this fact is available with a count of 100 or more or a quotable sentence (the Wikipedia article states one-sidedness only in the same terms). The far query is stored (non-orientable) and uses inheritance: the edit puts the strip in the class of two-sided surfaces, which are orientable in ordinary space. Its bridge is a fine point of topology and the check has not been audited on the four models (Rule 6 audit pending); if two or more miss it, the far query should be replaced by a simpler stored consequence. Derived: compositions with the parity and primality of the side count (2 is even, 2 is prime), a composition with a playing card (it has two sides), and an inheritance query: the surface shown in the three-arrow recycling symbol is a Möbius strip (the check), a member of the class the edit changes, so the rule passes to it. The prompt does not say "twisted band", which hinted at the original answer, and the answer rests on the logo being a Möbius strip, as the check states. The earlier colouring, ants and sheet-of-paper questions are gone: they are classroom demonstrations of one-sidedness, close to stored facts. The unrelated near query asks how many boundary edges the strip has (one, unaffected by the edit) instead of who it is named after, which contained its answer.
